"""Time the parts of gov.decisions.register.read on this worktree."""
import copy
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from gov.decisions import register
from gov.store.loader import _git, _register, _tree, register_entries

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
for _ in range(2):
    t = time.perf_counter(); head = _git(root, "rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD^{commit}"); t1 = time.perf_counter()
    tree = _tree(root); t2 = time.perf_counter()
    named = _register(root, tree); t3 = time.perf_counter()
    live = register_entries(named[1])[0]; t4 = time.perf_counter()
    reg = register.read(root); t5 = time.perf_counter()
    dup = copy.deepcopy(reg); t6 = time.perf_counter()
    print(f"rev-parse {t1-t:.4f} ls-tree {t2-t1:.4f} register-file {t3-t2:.4f} entries {t4-t3:.4f} "
          f"read {t5-t4:.4f} deepcopy {t6-t5:.4f} n={len(reg['entries'])}")

risks: The cache lives for the life of the process. A history rewrite that gives the same commit id gives the same content, so staleness is not possible by construction. Dropping it would save about 5 s over 360 calls but leave the cached value open to a future caller that changes it; I kept it.
